title: Estimating the Ultimate Shear Capacity of Composite Beam-Column Joints Under Seismic Loading Using Machine Learning Models
content: Beam–column joints represent one of the most critical and vulnerable regions in reinforced concrete frames subjected to seismic loading. Failure of these joints can significantly compromise the overall structural integrity of the system and may trigger progressive collapse during severe earthquakes. To enhance the seismic performance of beam–column joints, composite Steel Reinforced Concrete (SRC) systems have been increasingly adopted due to their superior strength, stiffness, and ductility characteristics. Despite their advantages, accurate prediction of the shear capacity of composite SRC beam–column joints remain a challenging task. The complexity arises from severe stress concentrations, nonlinear material behavior, and multidirectional force transfer mechanisms inherent in such connections. Furthermore, experimental investigations required to evaluate the seismic performance of these joints are often time-consuming and cost-consuming and costly, highlighting the need for reliable and cost-effective predictive approaches. This study presents the development of a machine learning-based predictive model for estimating the shear capacity of composite SRC beam–column joints subjected to seismic loading. A dataset comprising 25 experimentally tested specimens was utilized, covering a wide range of joint configurations, material properties, and loading conditions. The model incorporates 16 input parameters, including concrete compressive strength, steel yield strength, geometric characteristics of the joint, axial load ratio, steel section properties, column height, beam length, and joint classification (interior or exterior). The proposed model was trained and validated to predict the ultimate shear capacity of unseen cases accurately. The results demonstrated that the model successfully captured complex nonlinear interactions among the governing parameters and provided stable and consistent predictions across the entire dataset. Compared with conventional numerical approaches, which commonly exhibit coefficients of variation (COV) ranging from 100% to 169%, the proposed model achieved a significantly lower COV of approximately 30%. The findings of this study provide structural engineers with a practical and efficient predictive tool that can assist in the analysis and optimization of composite SRC beam–column joint design under seismic loading conditions.
